QF.id: Retirement Planning Products: National Pension System (NPS)_57

question.text: Annuity income received from NPS is treated for income-tax purposes as:

answer.text: Taxable as income in the hands of the annuitant in the year of receipt
Taxed only at a special concessional flat rate, separate from slab rates

explanation.text: The Logic: The NPS annuity is purchased out of the accumulated retirement corpus, and the periodic annuity payments that the annuitant receives are treated as taxable income in the hands of the annuitant in the year they are received. There is no general exemption for the ongoing annuity stream; only the original lump-sum withdrawal portion and corpus phase enjoy specific tax benefits under the prevailing NPS tax framework. The Trap: Annuity payments are not capital gains (they are a periodic income stream, not a sale of a capital asset), they are not exempt, and they are not taxed at a separate concessional flat rate carved out from normal slab rates. They are added to the annuitant's taxable income and taxed under normal rules. Note: The cited Series XVII pages (p.144-p.145, p.180-p.181) state that NPS annuity income is taxable as income in the hands of the annuitant, but they do not specifically classify it under the "salary income" head. The framing above therefore stays at the workbook-supported level — taxable in the annuitant's hands — rather than asserting a specific tax head not in the cited source.
